newsitem.title: GERMANY: German NATO workers find agreement on job cuts.
newsitem.headline: German NATO workers find agreement on job cuts.

text.p: Civilian workers at United States, British and other NATO bases in Germany have agreed compensation packages over planned job cuts, union officials said on Friday.
The agreement follows a demonstration in Bonn earlier this week by some seven thousand NATO employees and the resumption of strike action by some of the 35,000 staff employed by the NATO allies.

Under the settlement, employees losing their job will be offered either equivalent or acceptable employment elsewhere in the bases. Only when this is not possible will a redundancy cash payment be negotiated, a spokeswoman for the OeTV German public sector union said.
Many of the mostly German civilians working at the bases have already lost their jobs as NATO forces in Germany have been cut back since the end of the Cold War.
